PullRequest.Title: agentHost: native Mission Control environments
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Expose VS Code's existing native Agent Host utility process as an opt-in user-local Mission Control environment over Azure Web PubSub. Local sessions continue using local IPC; remote clients use the same native session state and protocol handler. No separate daemon is launched.

The URI prerequisite [#339492](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/339492) has merged. This PR now targets `main`, merged locally in `d9b4cd31dd3`.

- Register, heartbeat, withdraw and recover the environment using trusted local credentials, canonical-owner checks and a stable random profile-local compute identity.
- Enforce signed control, sealed identity/MCP authentication, lane/client-ID binding, passive access, relay workspace/resource grants, and host-management/root-configuration restrictions.
- Discover/connect to existing user-local environments with cached-first inventory and background refresh; retain the existing managed-sandbox flow.
- Mirror authoritative AHP actions and selected genuine SDK metadata with bounded spools, durable acknowledgements and signed retained backfill. Native titles and activity update MC's task catalog.
- Support the opt-in path in built desktop products as well as source builds, retaining the existing default-off experimental setting keys.
- Use product display names, ordinary Mission Control class/management names, and a scoped DI-backed native adapter. Node implementation lives under `node/missionControl/`.
- Consume negotiated standard session URIs from the prerequisite without global provider aliases or historical URI/storage rewriting.
- Keep host-wide diagnostic logs off relay ingress, backpressure mirror publication without dropping retained frames, bound unanswered AHP handshakes, and recover transient identity-validation faults without treating refused credentials as compatible.

No separate VS Code issue is linked; this is the user-local environment integration. Environment-management UX alongside SSH/dev tunnels is a separate follow-up.

## Security scope and remaining qualification

Remote owner access includes sessions, tools and granted workspace resources. MC stores mirrored conversation content; credential sealing is not conversation E2EE.

Mandatory handshake binding, per-client/session credential sponsorship, OS containment, response-part ID continuity and full durable AHP restart/history baselines remain accepted deferrals. Unbound sealed tokens remain replayable, active credentials use the existing shared native provider store, and path grants do not claim OS confinement.

See the [security requirements and sources](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/680d699afd12266e3e42d5fb2db6b4723f77178b/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/missionControl/MISSION_CONTROL_SECURITY_REQUIREMENTS.md), [remaining gaps](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/680d699afd12266e3e42d5fb2db6b4723f77178b/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/missionControl/MISSION_CONTROL_PRODUCTION_GAPS.md), and [operation/configuration](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/680d699afd12266e3e42d5fb2db6b4723f77178b/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/missionControl/MISSION_CONTROL.md). The source matrix groups 35 requirements by security topic and distinguishes Copilot Host contracts, protocol specifications, user choices and assistant-proposed adaptations. It was independently reviewed for clarity and pinned-source consistency.

GitHub-authoritative authorization expiry, durable per-session mirror opt-out, enterprise endpoint coherence/disclosure, and independent operator-owned session/repository policy remain identified gaps, not implicitly accepted deferrals.

An older signed macOS arm64 artifact passed registration, crypto loading, native/remote execution and withdrawal. Final-head packaged qualification, Windows/Linux and enterprise deployment, and completed three-hour reliability qualification remain outstanding. No review requirement or release/privacy approval is overridden by this PR.

## How to exercise

1. Sign in to GitHub in a desktop window and leave `chat.agentHost.experimentalMissionControlFakeEndpoint` empty.
2. Enable `chat.agentHost.experimentalMissionControl.enabled`, using the default trusted HTTPS endpoint.
3. Wait for `Mission Control ready; environmentId=...` in the Agent Host log.
4. Create/use a native session normally over local IPC.
5. From a separate matching-owner client, discover the environment, authenticate through the relay and list/open/drive that same session. In another VS Code instance, use **Connect to Mission Control Environment...**.
6. Verify task title/activity, disconnect/reconnect, and owner withdrawal. Offline user-local attachment does not provision replacement compute.

The local test-endpoint setting is only for a trusted loopback HTTP integration-test server; the local GitHub credential is sent there if explicitly configured.

## Validation

Current head: `680d699afd1`; the latest changes are documentation-only. Runtime code is unchanged from the tested implementation at `0622f8dd27e`. Client output was refreshed incrementally after merging `main`. Local validation:

- `npm run typecheck-client` — **passed**.
- `npm run test-node -- --runGlob '**/agentHost/test/node/{missionControl*,protocolServerHandler,copilotSessionLauncher}.test.js'` — **423 passed**.

- `npm run valid-layers-check` — **passed**.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/browser/agentHostProtocolClient.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/browser/webPubSubRelayTransport.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/protocolServerHandler.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/missionControl/missionControlAuthentication.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/missionControl/missionControlHost.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/missionControl/missionControlProtocolServer.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/missionControl/missionControlSessionMirror.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/browser/cloudSandboxAgentHostContribution.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxConnectionCustomization.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxApiService.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxTelemetry.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxConnectionCustomization.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts` — **passed**.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/protocolServerHandler.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostChatContribution.test.ts` — **passed**.
- `node build/lib/formatter.ts --replace --verify src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/agentHostProtocolClient.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/remoteAgentHost/test/browser/remoteAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts` — **passed**, formatting-only corrections.
- `git diff --cached --check` and normal commit hooks — **passed**.
- Documentation target resolution, all 35 sequential requirement IDs and cross-references — **passed**.

**Current-head CI passed:** [Code OSS](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37381170894) completed all 21 jobs successfully at `680d699afd1`, including compile/hygiene and Linux/macOS/Windows unit, integration, browser, smoke and remote tests. CodeQL, Component Fixtures/Screenshots, Monaco, chat-lib, telemetry, dependency, license and PR-policy checks also passed.

The [previous-head Code OSS run](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37375389714) was interrupted by killed lint/tsec processes, a browser-runner shutdown and a smoke-step deadline after 66 passing tests. The fresh run passed without changing runtime code or weakening any check or timeout.

Real isolated, sync-disabled two-instance runs exercised native remote turns and verified shell output in both host directions. A completed two-hour run recorded 2,470 snapshots, 15 remote turns, 71 verified terminals and eight deliberate same-client reconnects. Original-owner replay covered 92 sessions/184 snapshots, including a 1,546,452-byte chat. Held application subscriptions recovered across deliberate host socket loss in about 28.4 seconds with no subscription errors and subsequent remote work.

Unexpected host socket-close cause remains unconfirmed. A three-hour attempt was reboot-interrupted; its resumed run ended after about 104 minutes when the automation connection closed, with the apps/debugging endpoints still live afterward. Neither attempt completed three-hour qualification. These bounded observations are not fleet-stability or security certification.

(Written by Copilot)

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The single-outstanding-frame invariant, shared queue ownership, and ack-driven call path are explicit and test-covered. Exact RTT and action rate vary, affecting severity magnitude but not the throughput mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Web PubSub publish operations and the shared outbound frame queue
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For F outgoing AHP or mirror frames, completion now takes approximately F sequential Web PubSub acknowledgement round trips; all client lanes and mirror traffic share the same queue, so queued latency also grows with traffic from other sessions.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Remote session throughput is capped by relay acknowledgement latency, with head-of-line blocking and rising interactive response latency; bursts can fill the 512-frame queue and close the connection.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no native Mission Control server queue. The existing `WebPubSubRelayTransport.send` path sends every generated frame immediately and independently tracks all pending acknowledgement IDs, so relay throughput is not limited to one frame per acknowledgement RTT.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every AHP response, notification, chunk, and mirrored event is appended to one process-wide queue, but the new drain sends only one frame and then waits for its Web PubSub acknowledgement before sending the next frame.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `_drain` loop at line 290 is conditioned on `this._pending.size === 0`, adds exactly one ack ID to `_pending`, and is re-entered only when an acknowledgement deletes that ID. This new server is the PR's outbound Mission Control path.
Findings.Title: Allow more than one relay publish per acknowledgement RTT
Findings.Impact: On a realistic remote turn, streamed chat/actions and mirrored state generate many frames. With normal cloud RTT, each frame waits another RTT, and an interactive reply can sit behind mirror traffic from any session or lane.
Findings.Evidence: `MissionControlLane.send` routes all lanes through `_publish`/`_enqueue`; mirror events use the same `_enqueue`. `_receive` deletes one pending ack and invokes `_drain` again. The added test `serializes AHP publishes behind acknowledgements without reordering` explicitly proves that only the first of two responses is sent before the first ack. By contrast, `browser/webPubSubRelayTransport.ts:472-484` sends all chunks without waiting for prior acks.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve send order while allowing a bounded window of outstanding publishes, as the existing client transport does, and/or batch adjacent frames before crossing WPS. Keep the current queue byte limits and per-frame acknowledgement/error handling.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous call chain and repeated full-payload transformations are directly visible. Payload distributions determine the exact pause length, so severity is medium, but the per-action CPU/allocation mechanism is certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU time and temporary/retained strings, parsed objects, UTF-8 buffers, base64 buffers, and framed JSON
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows with every emitted state action and its payload size. Each envelope is stringified here, parsed back at line 250, stringified at least twice again by `chunk`, UTF-8 encoded, and then stringified once per retained frame.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: The Agent Host event loop is blocked by repeated serialization and allocation, increasing action/stream latency and CPU/GC pressure for both local IPC sessions and remote sessions while Mission Control is enabled.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before the PR, authoritative state emission did not synchronously clone, encode, chunk, and retain every envelope for Mission Control; normal local Agent Host dispatch only applied and emitted the action.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: With Mission Control enabled, the synchronous `Emitter.fire` call now runs `mirror.enqueue`, which performs a JSON round trip plus chunk/framing serialization before the state dispatch can return. `chunk` itself stringifies the payload and the single-frame envelope and encodes the string to UTF-8.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: This added line synchronously serializes each envelope admitted by the newly added `onDidEmitEnvelope` listener in `missionControlHost.ts:120-140`; that listener directly calls `mirror.enqueue` before returning.
Findings.Title: Move mirror serialization off the synchronous action path
Findings.Impact: Streaming responses, terminal data, large response parts, and history-loading actions can make local turns consume extra CPU and pause subsequent Agent Host work even though mirror network publication itself is scheduled later.
Findings.Evidence: `AgentHostStateManager._applyAndEmit` calls `_onDidEmitEnvelope.fire(envelope)` synchronously. The new listener calls `mirror.enqueue`; this method performs `JSON.stringify(envelope)`, `JSON.parse(serialised)`, `chunk(payload)`, and `_frameJson` for each fragment. `chunking.ts:97-119` confirms two further stringifications and a `TextEncoder.encode`, with base64 work for large payloads.
Findings.Recommendation: Make the event listener perform only bounded queue admission, then serialize/chunk in the scheduled mirror drain (or a worker). Serialize once and let chunking consume the serialized bytes instead of parsing and re-stringifying, while retaining the existing spool limits and failure signaling.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The per-request synchronous boundary and multiplicative root/ancestor scans are explicit. Filesystem speed and realistic root count vary, affecting magnitude but not the blocking mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Synchronous filesystem `realpath`, `stat`, and `lstat` operations on the Agent Host event loop
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For R remote resource operations, P missing path ancestors, and G current grant/workspace/content roots, authorization performs O(R × (P + G)) synchronous filesystem operations; `_resourceRoots` also rebuilds its roots by scanning all session summaries on each request.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Remote file reads/lists/writes incur added latency and can block unrelated local and remote Agent Host work, especially for tool bursts, many sessions/roots, missing paths, or slow/network-mounted filesystems.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, request dispatch did not run this synchronous canonicalization/grant scan. Resource handlers proceeded to their normal filesystem implementation without repeatedly canonicalizing every configured and session-derived root on the shared event loop.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every Mission Control resource request now synchronously resolves the target (or each missing ancestor), may synchronously stat it, reconstructs all granted roots from session summaries, and synchronously resolves each root until a match is found.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added relay authorization path invokes `_isGrantedRelayResource` before every request at `protocolServerHandler.ts:2007-2014`; line 2266 begins a synchronous ancestor walk, and line 2293 synchronously resolves every dynamically recomputed root.
Findings.Title: Avoid synchronous filesystem walks on every relay resource request
Findings.Impact: A remote agent commonly issues many file operations during a turn. These checks serialize filesystem waits on the single Agent Host thread and can make chat/tool progress stutter while also delaying local IPC sessions hosted by the same process.
Findings.Evidence: `_handleRequest` unconditionally calls `_requireRelayResourceAccess` for relay clients. File requests enter `_isGrantedRelayResource`, whose loop calls `realpathSync`, `statSync`, and potentially `lstatSync` per ancestor; its final `.some` invokes `relayResourceRoots`, which scans session summaries, then calls `realpathSync(root)` per root.
Findings.Recommendation: Cache canonical grant roots and session-derived content roots with invalidation on grants/session/workspace changes, and perform target canonicalization asynchronously while preserving the current missing-path and symlink checks.

Scenarios.Scenario: Enable the native Agent Host as a live Mission Control environment
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After-restored configuration resolves the local account, starts the Agent Host, crosses local management IPC, validates the GitHub owner, reads registration metadata/policy, registers over HTTPS, fetches signing keys, and joins WPS control/ingest groups before readiness. Historical SDK replay starts when the mirror is created but is not awaited by relay readiness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Configure Mission Control in the utility-process Agent Host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per coalesced configuration generation; workspace/account/setting events are throttled through one Throttler and the host uses a Sequencer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Mission Control configuration IPC existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the renderer considers configuration successful.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate the configured credential with the GitHub `/user` endpoint
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per fresh configuration and one per remote identity authentication handshake.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The native Agent Host did not validate an MC owner.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read or atomically create the stable profile-local compute identity
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per registration; first use additionally creates, syncs, renames, and cleans one temporary file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No compute identity file was accessed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register/heartbeat the environment, fetch JWKS, open WPS, and join bootstrap groups
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold enable uses registration plus JWKS plus WPS joins and an online heartbeat; steady state uses one heartbeat per minute, token refresh near expiry, and JWKS is cached for five minutes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No environment registration or host-side relay connection existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold registration/JWKS/WPS joins block readiness; periodic heartbeat/token work is outside normal local-turn critical paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configuration generations are coalesced; steady-state cost is fixed by heartbeat/token intervals, while cold metadata cost includes current session count and policy read.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Renderer updates use a Throttler; host configuration uses a Sequencer; check-ins for one generation are coalesced; registration metadata operations are sequential and individually timeout-bounded.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Signing keys are cached for five minutes, WPS credentials until near expiry, and the compute ID is persisted. Credential rejection stops retries; transient check-in failures back off to 30 seconds.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Network and provider-policy latency vary, but call counts and critical-path placement are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional report: the registration boundaries are bounded, coalesced, timeout-protected, and expected for the opt-in feature.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run local native agent turns while Mission Control mirroring is enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each authoritative state action is applied, then the synchronous `onDidEmitEnvelope` listener calls mirror admission before `dispatchServerAction` returns. WPS publication is scheduled later, but JSON cloning/chunking/framing is on the action path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stringify, parse, re-stringify, encode, optionally base64-chunk, frame, and retain every AHP envelope
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per authoritative action, with additional frame work per chunk; effective cost scales with total action payload bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: State actions were not synchronously transformed into MC mirror frames.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous CPU/allocation blocks subsequent Agent Host work even for local IPC sessions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish retained mirror frames to WPS and await transport and durable ingest acknowledgements
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least one WPS event per admitted frame; large actions are chunked. Durable ack controls retention.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No native state mirror network publication existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Publication is off the immediate local action critical path, but its globally serialized queue can contend with interactive remote replies.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Frequency and byte size of chat deltas/response parts, terminal data, tool actions, and history-loading actions; spool limits cap retention at 128 MiB/100,000 AHP frames globally.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Admission is synchronous and uncoalesced per action. Publication is scheduled, but only one shared WPS publish may be outstanding.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No serialization cache or action coalescing exists. Frames remain retained until durable ingest watermarks advance; reconnect reuses retained serialized frames.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact envelope sizes and action rates vary by provider and turn, but the repeated transformations and synchronous reachability are certain.

Scenarios.Scenario: Drive a native session remotely through a Mission Control relay
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A signed spawn opens a lane, initialize/authenticate completes over WPS, then requests reach ProtocolServerHandler. Outbound responses/notifications and mirror events enter one queue; file/resource requests synchronously authorize filesystem paths before their normal handlers run.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send AHP and mirror frames through Azure Web PubSub with per-frame acknowledgements
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One boundary operation per frame/chunk, globally across up to 32 lanes plus mirror traffic; only one is in flight.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No native host relay existed; the existing client relay transport sends generated frames without waiting for prior acks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Every remote response waits behind preceding frames and acknowledgement RTTs; this is directly on remote interaction progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate the remote owner's unsealed GitHub token
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One `/user` request per fresh relay identity handshake; MCP authentication follows only after identity succeeds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No host-side relay identity validation existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks handshake authentication, but is one bounded call rather than per AHP action.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronously canonicalize the requested path/ancestors and every current grant root
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per resource operation; target work scales with missing ancestor depth and grant checks scale with workspace/session/content-root count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Resource requests did not perform this relay-specific synchronous filesystem scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks request dispatch and the shared Agent Host event loop before the actual file operation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of streamed AHP frames, concurrent lanes/sessions, mirror backlog, resource requests per tool turn, missing path depth, and current session-derived roots.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Inbound lanes can coexist, but all outbound traffic is globally serialized to one unacknowledged frame. Filesystem authorization is synchronous, so concurrent requests serialize on the event loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache exists for canonical grant roots or target paths. Relay lane state is bounded and idle-expired; authentication replay maps are bounded.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cloud RTT and filesystem latency vary, but the one-frame window and repeated synchronous calls are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable network throughput/head-of-line blocking and synchronous filesystem regressions submitted.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reconcile persisted SDK metadata for existing sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Mirror creation enumerates all known sessions and schedules each source. Up to four workers open per-session metadata databases, reserve sequence ranges, then stream the provider journal from the beginning to reconcile the cursor/latest title/state. This work is not awaited by environment readiness but shares process CPU, disk, and spool/network capacity.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/write per-session sequence and journal-cursor metadata
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold source setup performs metadata reads and one reservation write per observed session; later writes occur when durable SDK acks advance cursors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No MC SDK sequence/cursor metadata existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off registration and local AHP critical paths, though it shares the Agent Host process.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stream and parse the Copilot session journal
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-prefix scan per observed session when no cursor exists or to locate a persisted cursor; total bytes scale with accumulated session journals.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing journals were not scanned for Mission Control metadata replication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background work; not awaited by relay readiness or local dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronize a changed catalog title through the provider runtime RPC
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per source title change after comparison.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Host catalog titles were not synchronized for MC metadata replication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs in the source worker, not the local state-action critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of existing sessions and total journal bytes; effective history publication is constrained by spool capacity and durable acknowledgements.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A shared Limiter caps source workers at four; each session has one drain; replay waits for capacity rather than spawning more work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Durable sequence reservations and acked journal cursors support warm restart, but locating a cursor still scans from the journal start. Queues and memory are bounded.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the work, moderate for user-visible impact.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large profiles can cause significant background I/O, but the work is opt-in, concurrency-limited, streamed, and off the readiness/turn critical path; concrete user-visible degradation is less certain than the reported issues.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: eager history work is bounded in concurrency and off the main critical path; magnitude is insufficiently established for another high-confidence regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Mission Control environment picker and connect to another user-local host
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The picker gets the local environment ID over IPC, renders a fresh cached inventory if present, performs one forced HTTPS refresh in the background, then fetches the selected environment and mints/connects relay credentials.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the local host's environment ID

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One forced refresh per picker invocation; ordinary callers reuse a 60-second account-generation cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cached items display first; refresh is background unless no cache exists.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch selected environment and establish the WPS client connection
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One environment GET and one connection credential/relay flow per accepted selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No user-local environment attachment flow existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks completion of the connect command, as expected.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Inventory item count affects one filter/sort/map pass; connection cost is one selected environment.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A picker owns one refresh cancellation token; connection setup is sequential. The inventory service does not coalesce arbitrary simultaneous forced refreshes, but the changed product path has one refresh.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Inventory is cached for 60 seconds and invalidated by account generation; stale cache is shown immediately while refresh runs.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Inventory size and network latency vary, but there is no demonstrated fan-out or hot repetition in the changed caller.
Scenarios.Verdict: No report: cached-first rendering and one background refresh keep discovery bounded.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full 87-file inventory and relevant production diffs. Submitted three findings: globally ack-serialized WPS output, synchronous repeated mirror serialization on every state action, and synchronous repeated filesystem authorization on each relay resource request. Registration, discovery, credential refresh, bounded spools, cleanup, cache behavior, and historical replay were also traced; no concrete regression fix requiring blame was identified.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
